svg.title: How the weight on a zone's own mean depends on its sample size and on tau
svg.desc: Weight on a zone's own survey average plotted against the number of households, for three population spreads. The curve for tau = 8 passes through one half at nine households and reaches 0.959 at 210 households.
svg.text: Small groups shrink more, and tau decides how much
Weight on the zone's own mean is tau squared divided by (tau squared plus the squared standard error). With sigma = 24 and tau = 8 it is n divided by (n plus 9).
weight on the zone's own mean
The black marks are the eight zones. Let tau fall toward zero and every weight falls toward zero, which is complete pooling.
Let tau grow and every weight rises toward one, which is no pooling. Nothing about the households changed; only the assumed spread across zones did.
The nine in n plus 9 is sigma squared divided by tau squared: the population distribution is worth nine households in every zone.
